newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends up on stocks factor.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends up on stocks factor.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended higher after a decline in supply of raw materials, but consumer demand was still weak owing to the holiday season, traders said.
"The market is featureless, with both physical and paper (futures) prices adjusting to each other," said a trader.
He added that trading was "practically non-existent" as regular overseas buyers were mostly on holiday.
At the close, the MRELB quoted January RSS1 buyer at 316 cents ($1.25) a kg, half cent up from Tuesday. January SMR 20 buyer ended a cent higher at 306.50.
Traders offered the SMR CV at 362 cents, SMR L at 342, SMR 5 at 317, SMR 10 at 306, SMR 20 at 305 and drum latex at 235.
They attributed the market's current level to a drop in stocks of raw materials due to rains in the past fortnight.
"Producers are not desperate to sell because they don't have too much stocks on their hands," said another trader.
"Otherwise, prices would be coming down further."
The INRO five-day moving average fell to 240.46 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Dec 10 from 240.76 on Dec 9. The daily indicator price rose to 240.29 from 239.91.
